_readme: TO SEND JESSE A FILE: drop it in this folder and push. That is the whole
process -- the rail lists whatever is in here, so a file with no entry
below still shows up, just under its own filename with no description.
Add an entry here only when the filename alone is not enough. Order in
this file is the order in the rail; anything unlisted sorts after, newest
Nothing in this folder is reachable over the web. netlify.toml 404s the
path, and the only way in is /api/jesse/file, which checks the session
cookie first. That is deliberate: it is the same door as the messages.
The notes below are served ONLY to an authenticated caller, which is why
the RAM instructions live here rather than in jesse.html -- anything in
that page is readable by anyone who guesses the URL, without a PIN.
The keys under "files" are exact filenames. "password" is shown in the
rail in plain text -- it is a convenience for a zip, not a secret.

ram-report.zip.label: RAM report script
ram-report.zip.note: Right-click the zip and Extract All (password below), then double-click ram-report.bat. A black window opens and prints the answer, and saves ram-report.txt to your Desktop — paste what's in it into the thread. Windows may warn you: that is only because the file came from the internet. Click More info, then Run anyway. It only reads what Windows already knows about your memory; it installs nothing and never touches the internet. You can read the whole thing first — right-click, Open with, Notepad. Get in the habit of doing that with anything you download. Including from me.

ram-report.bat.label: RAM report script (loose .bat)
ram-report.bat.note: Same thing, not zipped, in case the zip is a hassle. If it will not run, right-click it and choose Run as administrator. Or grab CPU-Z from cpuid.com — the SPD tab names every slot, even the empty ones. Or just call me.
